facts.statement: Procariama lived in Argentina between 11 and 2 million years ago during the Late Miocene and Late Pliocene.
facts.quote: Procariama is an extinct monotypic genus of phorusrhacid, which lived from the Late Miocene to the Late Pliocene (11-2 million years ago) of Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Procariama have been found in the Cerro Azul and Andalhuala Formations.
facts.quote: Fossils of the animal have been found in six places, in the Cerro Azul and Andalhuala Formations.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in the Andagalá and northern Belén departments of Catamarca province, and one site in La Pampa province.
facts.quote: More specifically in the Andagalá department and in the north of the Belén department of the Catamarca province, with a single location in the La Pampa province.

facts.statement: The genus Procariama was first described by Cayetano Rovereto in 1914.
facts.quote: The genus name was first published in 1914 by Cayetano Rovereto in Anales del Museo Nacional de Historia Natural.

facts.statement: Procariama stood about 70 cm tall and weighed approximately 10 kg.
facts.quote: Reaching about 70 cm in height and 10 kg in body mass, Procariama was one of the smaller phorusrhacids.

facts.statement: Procariama had a more robust build than Psilopterus, characterized by comparatively shorter thigh bones.
facts.quote: This more robust build can be attributed to a slight difference in the ratio between the bones of the legs, with the thigh being comparatively shorter in Procariama.

facts.statement: The hypotarsus of Procariama's tarsometatarsus features two protrusions, one lateral and one medial, near the proximal end.
facts.quote: In the tarsometatarsus, the hypotarsus has two protrusions, one laterally and one medially, in its most proximal portion.

facts.statement: The genus name Procariama means "before Cariama", referring to the red-legged seriema, its closest living relative.
facts.quote: The genus name of the animal means "before Cariama", referring to the genus Cariama, the red-legged seriema, which is a genus of small, carnivorous bird native to South America.

facts.statement: Procariama belongs to the order Cariamiformes, whose only modern representatives are seriemas.
facts.quote: Like all phorusrhacids, Procariama is part of the order Cariamiformes, the only modern representatives of which are the seriemas.

facts.statement: In 2024, Procariama was reclassified as a member of the subfamily Psilopterinae.
facts.quote: In 2024, it was reclassified as a member of the Psilopterinae.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Procariama as Mesembriornithinae.
Procariama is classified within the family Phorusrhacidae.
The Paleobi Database records the time range of Procariama as the Tortonian to Zanclean stages (8 to 3.8 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Zanclean (8 to 3.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Three additional specimens of Procariama are known besides the lectotype.
facts.quote: Three specimens of Procariama are known in addition to the lectotype.

facts.statement: Specimen FM-P 14525 is an exquisitely preserved and nearly complete skeleton of Procariama.
facts.quote: Secondly we have FM-P 14525, an exquisitely preserved and nearly complete skeleton.

rejected.statement: Procariama was larger than Psilopterus, Paleopsilopterus, and other members of the subfamily Psilopterinae.
rejected.quote: However, it was larger than Psilopterus, Paleopsilopterus, and other members of the subfamily Psilopterinae.
